## `mainframe.host.channel.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.channel.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The average fraction of time all channel paths in the Central Processing Complex (CPC) were busy processing I/O, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [1] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[1]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC metric group `cpc-usage-overview` field `channel-usage` (classic mode). The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. This is a system-wide average across all channel path identifiers (CHPIDs). For per-CHPID granularity use `mainframe.channel.utilization` instead.



## `mainframe.host.cpu.active.count`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.cpu.active.count` | UpDownCounter | `{cpu}` | The number of active processors of the specified type installed in the Central Processing Complex (CPC). [2] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[2]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC object properties `processor-count-<type>` (all modes), one data point per processor type in `mainframe.cpu.type`: `processor-count-general-purpose` (`cp`), `processor-count-ifl` (`ifl`), `processor-count-icf` (`icf`), `processor-count-iip` (`iip`), `processor-count-service-assist` (`sap`) and `processor-count-cbp` (`cbp`, Container Based Processors). The CBP property exists only for SE versions 2.14.0 through 2.15.0; collectors check for its presence before reading it. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to the physical CPU core count of a server, split by processor specialisation.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.cpu.type`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-cpu-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The type of mainframe processor within the Central Processing Complex (CPC). | `all`; `cp`; `icf` |

---

`mainframe.cpu.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aap` | Application Assist Processor (AAP), a processor dedicated to accelerating Java and XML processing for database workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `all` | All types of mainframe processors combined. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cbp` | Container Based Processor (CBP), a processor type for container-based workloads. Present only in HMC/SE versions 2.14.0 through 2.15.0. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `cp` | Central Processor (CP), the general-purpose processor that hosts a mainframe operating system such as z/OS. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `icf` | Integrated Coupling Facility (ICF), a processor dedicated to running coupling facility workloads for high-speed communication between systems in a sysplex. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ifl` | Integrated Facility for Linux (IFL), a processor dedicated to running Linux workloads on the mainframe. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `iip` | z Integrated Information Processor (zIIP), a processor dedicated to offloading eligible workloads such as Java applications from general-purpose processors. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `sap` | System Assist Processor (SAP), a processor dedicated to system management and I/O processing workloads. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.host.cpu.defective.count`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.cpu.defective.count` | UpDownCounter | `{cpu}` | The number of defective processors in the Central Processing Complex (CPC). [3] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[3]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC object property `processor-count-defective` (all modes). Defective processors are hardware-detected faulty units taken offline by the machine firmware. A non-zero value indicates a hardware service event should be investigated.



## `mainframe.host.cpu.spare.count`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.cpu.spare.count` | UpDownCounter | `{cpu}` | The number of spare processors available in the Central Processing Complex (CPC). [4] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[4]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC object property `processor-count-spare` (all modes). Spare processors are installed but unallocated units held in reserve for capacity-on-demand or defect replacement. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to hot-spare CPU cores in a high-availability server.



## `mainframe.host.cpu.utilization`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | The fraction of time processors of the specified type in the Central Processing Complex (CPC) were busy, as a ratio from 0 (idle) to 1 (fully utilised). [5] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[5]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC metric group `cpc-usage-overview` (classic mode). The group reports one field per processor type and sharing mode: `<type>-all-processor-usage`, `<type>-shared-processor-usage` and `<type>-dedicated-processor-usage` for each of cp, ifl, icf and iip. Select the field using the `mainframe.cpu.type` attribute, and `mainframe.cpu.sharing.mode` where set (the `-all-` field is the aggregate across both sharing modes). The HMC reports an integer percentage (0-100), which is divided by 100 to yield the 0-1 ratio this metric declares. A value of -1 indicates no processors of the specified type are installed. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to `system.cpu.utilization` aggregated across all cores of a given type.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.cpu.type`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-cpu-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The type of mainframe processor within the Central Processing Complex (CPC). | `all`; `cp`; `icf` |
| [`mainframe.cpu.sharing.mode`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-cpu-sharing-mode) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Opt-In` | string | The sharing mode of the mainframe processor — whether it is dedicated to one partition or shared across multiple partitions. | `all`; `dedicated`; `shared` |

---

`mainframe.cpu.sharing.mode` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | All mainframe processors, both shared and dedicated. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `dedicated` | The processor is dedicated to a specific partition and cannot be shared with other partitions. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `shared` | The processor can be shared among multiple partitions and is not dedicated to a specific partition. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.host.memory.size`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.memory.size` | Gauge | `By` | The size of memory of the specified category in the Central Processing Complex (CPC), in bytes. [6] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[6]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC object properties (all modes) via GET /api/cpcs/{cpc-id}: `storage-total-installed` (type=total), `storage-hardware-system-area` (type=hsa), `storage-customer` (type=partitions), `storage-customer-central` (type=central), `storage-customer-expanded` (type=expanded), and `storage-customer-available` (type=available). Use `mainframe.memory.type` to select the category.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.memory.type`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-memory-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The category of mainframe memory being measured within the Central Processing Complex (CPC). | `total`; `HSA`; `partitions` |

---

`mainframe.memory.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `available` | Memory not yet allocated to any active logical partition (LPAR) and available for assignment. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `central` | Memory allocated as central storage across all active logical partitions (LPARs) in the CPC. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `expanded` | Memory allocated as expanded storage across all active logical partitions (LPARs) in the CPC. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `HSA` | Memory reserved for the Hardware System Area (HSA), used for system management and I/O processing by the machine firmware. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `partitions` | Memory available for use by logical partitions (LPARs) running on the CPC. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `total` | Total amount of installed physical memory in the CPC. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `mainframe.host.memory.vfm.increment.size`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.memory.vfm.increment.size` | Gauge | `By` | The size of one IBM Virtual Flash Memory (VFM) increment in the Central Processing Complex (CPC), in bytes. [7] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[7]:** Virtual Flash Memory (VFM) is allocated in fixed-size increments. This metric reports the granularity step for VFM allocation changes. Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC object property `storage-vfm-increment-size` (all modes).



## `mainframe.host.memory.vfm.size`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `mainframe.host.memory.vfm.size` | Gauge | `By` | The total size of installed IBM Virtual Flash Memory (VFM) in the Central Processing Complex (CPC), in bytes. [8] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[8]:** Reported by the IBM Z HMC Web Services API CPC object property `storage-vfm-total` (SE >= 2.14.0) via GET /api/cpcs/{cpc-id}. IBM Virtual Flash Memory (VFM) is a solid-state storage tier extending addressable memory beyond physical DRAM.
